title: API Token Controls
scope: Admin controls, logging and revocation for API credentials on SaaS platforms. Sourced from vendor documentation; not an audit of any tenant.

definitions.excluded: The named control explicitly does not cover this credential.

providers.name: Zendesk Support
providers.scope_notes: Check IP entitlement and OAuth client creation date/type. API-token retirement applies to Support/Ticketing, Help Center and Voice; other Zendesk products differ.

controls.name: Allow API token access
controls.what: Turning it off makes all API tokens stop working until re-enabled.
controls.setting: Admin Center > Apps and integrations > APIs > API configuration
controls.quote: When you turn off token access, your tokens stop working. You’ll need to turn token access back on to reactivate them.

controls.name: Deactivate / delete API token
controls.what: Deactivating a token makes calls with it fail immediately; deleting is permanent.
controls.setting: Admin Center > Apps and integrations > APIs > API tokens
controls.quote: As soon as you deactivate a token, API calls using that token begin failing.

controls.name: IP restrictions
controls.what: Blocks API calls, sign-ins and page access from outside allowed IPs; customers (not agents/admins) can be exempted.
controls.quote: This means that any attempt to make API calls, sign in, or access pages in any Zendesk product will fail from outside your allowed IP addresses.

no_control.what: API tokens cannot be tied to a user or scoped; any verified user can use any token.
no_control.quote: Each API token can be used by any verified user on the account and isn't associated with a specific user.

no_control.what: From Apr 30 2027 admins cannot reactivate tokens at all (vendor retirement; new creation blocked from Oct 27 2026).
no_control.quote: All remaining API tokens will be deactivated permanently. Admins cannot reactivate tokens, and the API token management pages will be removed from Admin Center.

controls_unknown: No account-wide switch to disable OAuth found; OAuth "is managed separately" from the API configuration page.
Whether admins can block or scope third-party global OAuth clients (marketplace apps) beyond deleting their tokens.
Whether requiring SSO affects API token or OAuth token use.
Plan requirement for the Manage APIs custom-role permission (custom roles are typically Enterprise) not confirmed.

authentication.summary: OAuth bearer: authorization code or client credentials. Legacy API tokens via Basic email/token are being retired; unavailable to accounts created from 28 July 2026.

federation.details: This path uses a local/static or platform-native credential. Evaluate a separate federation path where listed.

ip_restriction.boundary: Account IP restrictions cover API/mobile/web access. Customer bypass and unsupported-endpoint exceptions require review.

renewal.summary: The static token is reused until it goes 30 days unused (deactivated, deleted after 60 more days) or is revoked. New creation stops 27 October 2026; all tokens stop working 30 April 2027. Accounts created on/after 28 July 2026 cannot use them.

administration.summary: OAuth scopes and user roles, API-token management, client/token revocation, SSO and IP policy.
administration.conditions: Check IP entitlement and OAuth client creation date/type. API-token retirement applies to Support/Ticketing, Help Center and Voice; other Zendesk products differ.

offboard.details: An API token is account-level and can act as any user, so it is not tied to one user's account.

inventory.details: Admin Center > Apps and integrations > APIs > API tokens lists all tokens.

reads.ui: Admin Center > Account > Logs > Access log > Filter: Category = Users, Summary = Show user; Authorization type = basic

token_format.notes: Sent as Basic auth '{email_address}/token:{api_token}'. Not tied to a user: any verified user's email works. No expiry; auto-deactivates after 30 days unused (from 2026-07-28). Creation blocked from 2026-10-27; all tokens stop 2027-04-30.

log_sources.name: Zendesk Audit Logs (/api/v2/audit_logs)
log_sources.notes: Enterprise; kept indefinitely. source_type 'apitoken' covers token create/deactivate/reactivate/delete. Admin Center token menu > View audit log.

log_sources.name: Zendesk Access Logs (/api/v2/access_logs)
log_sources.notes: ADPP add-on; 90 days; authorization_type 'basic' on token requests; user_id is the email used, not the token.

anomaly_cues: Basic-auth requests with a user_id that never used the integration (token works with any verified user's email)

containment.steps: Admin Center > Apps and integrations > APIs > API tokens: Deactivate (immediate), then Delete. Consider turning off API token access and migrating to OAuth.
containment.notes: Docs: 'As soon as you deactivate a token, API calls using that token begin failing.' Deactivated tokens can be reactivated until deleted.
